pages.title: Testing and Continuous Delivery of Software

evidence.quote: Quality assurance starts when requirements are written and continues throughout design, implementation, integration, and deployment.
Automated unit tests verify small components, while integration tests check whether services and modules interact correctly.
Sustainable engineering also requires maintainable code, clear documentation, controlled technical debt, and attention to the long-term cost of operating the software.

Continuous delivery extends this process by making releases small, repeatable, and reversible. Teams can use staging environments, versioned artifacts, deployment approvals, monitoring, and rollback procedures.

Cloud providers rent computing resources over the network.
Edge and fog computing move part of the work closer to sensors and devices, which reduces delay and the amount of data sent over long distances. Internet of Things devices rely on this model.

evidence.quote: Machine learning can be used to classify, rank, cluster, or search textual information.
while more recent approaches can represent sentences or documents using dense embeddings.
Text models can reproduce bias present in their data, and apparently strong accuracy can hide poor performance for a minority class.
Responsible evaluation therefore includes error analysis, representative test data, and documentation of limitations.
Predictions should be treated as evidence to support a decision rather than as unquestionable truth.

pages.title: Scalable and Fault-Tolerant Distributed Systems
pages.note: The primary competency is the only suggestion. The plausible secondary was not returned, so there was nothing extra to judge.

evidence.quote: Distributed software is composed of multiple processes or services that cooperate across machines or execution environments.
Scalability means that a system can handle larger workloads without an unacceptable loss of performance.

Systems should detect failed instances, retry operations safely, avoid duplicate side effects, and recover state after interruption. Timeouts, idempotent requests, health checks, graceful degradation, and monitored failover are common design techniques.
